Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. TempoHealth is close to committing, but our SRE and product teams have one hard requirement for go-live: a contract-level p95 response floor of <=100ms for our clinical inference route (patient-triage model). This is higher than your standard plans and would be scoped to Peak Window A (weekdays 8am-6pm PT).

Can Redwood approve a custom SLA carveout for this route? We understand there are operational costs and will sign a higher committed spend if needed. I attached our internal latency requirements sheet.

- Formal SLA language we can include in the MSA (p95, measurement method, exclusion windows)
- An operational runbook describing on-call, escalation, and warm standby behavior
- Commitment on whether you can provide a dedicated pool or guaranteed capacity during peak hours

We'd like to get this resolved within two weeks to align with our procurement calendar.

Appreciate a quick confirmation that we can evaluate this and the list of what you need from us.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera

Folks — summary from product feasibility review (engineering consulted):

Short answer: Likely achievable with a hybrid approach. Details: 
- Model variant: a trimmed & FP16-quant variant of their chosen model reduces per-token time. Estimated improvement: ~20-30% latency. Need to verify no model-quality regression on their eval set.
- Routing: Priority routing + pre-warmed workers for Peak Window A can reliably hit p95 <=100ms for steady 300 qps if we reserve ~6x baseline workers during the window. That implies approx. a 2.4x cost uplift for the hours reserved.
- KV/prefix caching: If their usage has high prefix reuse (which Alex please confirm), we can get an additional 10-15% reduction.
- Observability: We'll need to surface p95 measured at API gateway, with downstream breakdown (queueing, compute, network).

Questions for TempoHealth (Alex):
1) Can you share an eval prompt set (50–200 requests) so we can run a latency-quality regression on the quantized variant?
2) Confirm expected qps distribution across the Peak Window hours (is it backloaded or steady?).
3) Are there regulatory constraints requiring data residency during peak?

Operational caveats: Dedicated pool is the cleanest SLAM, but operationally we can do priority routing + warm standby if TempoHealth signs a capacity-commitment clause. Need legal signoff on measurement method (we measure at ingress).

I'll put a short tech note together and attach an initial ops-runbook draft.

— Grace
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: TempoHealth request: sub-100ms p95 carveout for clinical inference — proposed next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear requirements and for working quickly with us. We have a proposed path forward: 

1) Technical path: priority routing + warm standby during Peak Window A, combined with a quantized model variant. This avoids needing a fully dedicated pool while meeting p95 <=100ms in our sims given your expected load.
2) Commercial: Redwood requests a 12-month committed addendum at a 30% uplift to cover reserved capacity costs.
3) Measurement and exclusions: p95 measured at Redwood API ingress, rolling 7-day window for reporting; exclusions will include force majeure and scheduled maintenance windows with 72-hour advance notice.
4) Operational: we attached a draft runbook and redlined SLA for your procurement team to review.

Attachments: redlines_tempohealth_v1.pdf (showing our proposed SLA language and measurement clauses); sla-op-runbook-draft.md

Next actions:
- Alex: please send a 50–200 sample prompt set and confirm qps distribution by EOD Friday (2026-11-05).
- TempoHealth procurement: we'll accept redline comments within 5 business days once you confirm the mutual action plan.
- Internal: Priyom will own the MAP; Grace and Lauren/Stephanie will finalize technical runbook; Legal will be looped by EOD Monday for measurement language.

If TempoHealth agrees to the capacity-commitment addendum we'll provision the warm-standby policy and schedule a 1-hour technical kickoff next week.

Thanks all — I'll follow up with a one-page MAP and timeline later today.

Best,
Mike Grant
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
